title: Cleanaway Waste Management Ltd - Contract Resources Group Pty Ltd

timeline.event: ACCC commenced informal review under the Informal Merger Review Process Guidelines.
Former provisional date for announcement of findings (10 July 2025) brought forward to 4 July 2025. ACCC announced it would not oppose the proposed acquisition.

body_sections.Summary: Cleanaway Waste Management Ltd ( Cleanaway ) proposes to acquire 100 per cent of Contract Resources Group Pty Ltd ( Contract Resources ) (the Proposed Acquisition ). Contract Resources’ current majority shareholders are two private equity firms, SCF Partners Inc and Viburnum Funds Pty Ltd. Cleanaway is an Australian-based recycling, waste management, and industrial services company. Contract Resources is a specialist provider of industrial services for complex and high value assets in the energy and oil and gas sector. Industrial services involve the provision of maintenance and cleaning services to industrial facilities, plants, and equipment, with many customers for these services operating in the mining, infrastructure, and oil and gas sectors. Cleanaway and Contract Resources each provide a range of industrial services, including high pressure water services, vacuum loading, non-destructive digging, cold cutting, tank cleaning and maintenance, emergency response, and decontamination and chemical cleaning. Contract Resources also provides more specialist industrial services such as catalyst handling and specialised mechanical services. Contract Resources also has a specialist waste processing facility in Gap Ridge, WA, which is used for processing hazardous materials including mercury-impacted waste.
body_sections.Market definition: The ACCC considered the effect of the proposed acquisition on: the supply of one or more industrial services, and the supply of waste management services (including the collection, processing/treatment, and/or disposal of various waste streams generated by industrial customers) on a regional, state and national basis. For the purposes of this assessment, the ACCC did not need to reach a concluded view on the boundaries of the relevant markets.
body_sections.Competition analysis: The ACCC concluded that the proposed acquisition was unlikely to substantially lessen competition in any market in Australia. The ACCC found that Contract Resources is primarily a provider of specialist industrial services such as catalyst handling, which Cleanaway does not supply. While Cleanaway and Contract Resources overlap in the supply of other types of industrial services, particularly to customers in the oil and gas sector, the ACCC concluded that post acquisition Cleanaway would likely be competitively constrained by alternative suppliers of these services. In addition, key customers would likely have countervailing power due to their ability to bypass the merged entity – for example, by sponsoring new entry or sponsoring the expansion of existing rivals. The ACCC also considered whether Cleanaway would be able to profitably leverage Contract Resources’ strong position in the supply of a specialist industrial service, such as catalyst handling, to advantage Cleanaway’s waste management offering. For example, this could occur by requiring customers to acquire a bundle of specialist industrial services and waste management services, lessening competition in the supply of such services. The ACCC concluded that it was unlikely that Cleanaway would be able to profitably adopt such a strategy as customers would have the ability to not accept a bundled offering due to the alternative sources of supply available to them, including through sponsoring new entry. In addition, any loss of sales to customers that accepted such a bundle was unlikely to make rival waste management companies less competitive, given their broad customer base includes many customers who do not acquire specialist industrial services.
